metadata.description: Curated registry of high-value OneStop and CSE pages for the UMN CS Grad advisor. Each entry is a stub: what the page covers, its URL, owning office, and whether to ingest the full content or only reference it.
metadata.ingestion_strategy: Pages marked 'ingest: true' should be scraped and added to the RAG knowledge base. Pages marked 'reference_only: true' should be represented as stubs with URL + description — do not ingest full text as it changes frequently.

pages.title: Academic Calendar
pages.stub_description: UMN Twin Cities academic calendar with term start/end dates, drop/add deadlines, registration windows, final exam times, and financial aid timeline. Always direct students here for current-term dates.
pages.bot_use: Direct students here for any date/deadline question. Do not state specific dates without this source — they change each term.

pages.title: Drop/Add Deadlines
pages.stub_description: Term-specific deadlines for adding, dropping, and withdrawing from courses, including tuition refund cutoffs and W-grade deadlines.
pages.bot_use: Quote general policy (e.g., 'drop without W is typically end of week 2') but always direct to this page for current dates.

pages.title: Register for Classes
pages.stub_description: How to register for classes at UMN: self-service registration in MyU, class permission numbers, waitlists, time conflicts, registration rules for grad students.
pages.bot_use: Use for registration how-to questions. Registration rules section is useful for CS grad students.

pages.title: Registration Times (Appointment Times)
pages.stub_description: Explains how registration appointment times are assigned by credit count and student type. Students check their specific time in MyU.
pages.bot_use: Explain that appointment times are assigned by credit count and found in MyU. Direct here for details.

pages.title: Holds on Student Account
pages.stub_description: Types of registration and financial holds at UMN, how to check holds in MyU, which office resolves each hold type.
pages.bot_use: Use to answer 'why can't I register' or 'I have a hold' questions. Provides office routing by hold type.

pages.title: Class Permission Numbers
pages.stub_description: When and how to get a class permission number (consent code) from instructors or departments to register for closed, restricted, or instructor-consent courses.
pages.bot_use: Use for 'how do I get a permission number' questions.

pages.title: Wait Lists
pages.stub_description: How UMN course waitlists work, how students get moved from waitlist to enrolled, and what to do if waitlist doesn't resolve.
pages.bot_use: Use for waitlist-related registration questions.

pages.title: Grad and Professional: Degree Completion Steps
pages.stub_description: University-level steps for graduate degree completion: GPAS, declaring graduation month, thesis submission, oral exam, change of degree award date.
pages.bot_use: Use for university-level graduation process questions. CS-specific requirements come from CS handbook.

pages.title: GPAS – Graduate Planning and Audit System
pages.stub_description: What GPAS is, how to access it in MyU, how to read the audit, and what to do if there are discrepancies.
pages.bot_use: Use for 'what is GPAS', 'how do I check my degree progress', 'GPAS says I'm missing X' questions.

pages.title: Graduation Steps (Graduate Students)
pages.stub_description: Step-by-step university process to apply for graduation: submitting month of intended graduation, GPAS clearance, ceremony registration.
pages.bot_use: Use alongside CS handbook to answer graduation process questions.

pages.title: Transcripts
pages.stub_description: How to order official and unofficial transcripts, processing times, costs, electronic vs. paper delivery.
pages.bot_use: Use for transcript request questions.

pages.title: Verify Enrollment
pages.stub_description: How to get an enrollment verification letter (for employers, insurance, visa, etc.) via OneStop or National Student Clearinghouse.
pages.bot_use: Use for 'I need proof of enrollment' or 'how do I show I'm enrolled full-time' questions.

pages.title: Full-Time Credits (Graduate)
pages.stub_description: Definition of full-time enrollment for graduate students at UMN, typically 6+ credits per semester. Relevant for financial aid, visa status, and tuition benefit eligibility.
pages.bot_use: Use for full-time enrollment definition questions. ALWAYS escalate international student implications to ISSS.

pages.title: Exception to Policy Petition
pages.stub_description: When and how to file a university-level exception to policy petition (e.g., retroactive add/drop, late withdrawal). Separate from CS department petitions.
pages.bot_use: Use for university-level exception questions. CS-specific petitions go through cs_grad.

pages.title: Leave of Absence
pages.stub_description: Process to request a leave of absence from UMN: eligibility, how to apply, implications for financial aid and enrollment. International students must contact ISSS.
pages.bot_use: Use for LOA questions. Always add ISSS escalation note for international students.

pages.title: Transfer Credit (Graduate)
pages.stub_description: University-level policies on transfer credit for graduate students. CS-specific transfer credit policy is more restrictive — always cross-reference CS handbook.
pages.bot_use: Use alongside CS handbook. Hard escalation to cs_grad for any specific transfer credit determination.

pages.title: Contact One Stop
pages.stub_description: OneStop contact info: phone 612-624-1111, in-person locations (Coffey Hall, West Bank Skyway, Bruininks Hall), hours, and online chat/appointment options.
pages.bot_use: Always include this when routing to OneStop.

pages.title: CSE Graduate: Current Students
pages.stub_description: CSE college-level resources for current grad students: forms, policies, funding, professional development, and contact info.
pages.bot_use: Use for CSE-level policy questions and forms not covered in the CS department handbook.

pages.title: CSE Academic Probation and Dismissal Policy
pages.stub_description: CSE college-level policy on academic probation, dismissal, and reinstatement for graduate students. Triggered by GPA falling below 3.0 or other conditions.
pages.bot_use: Hard escalation required. Use only for explaining general policy, never for individual standing assessment.

pages.title: CS Graduate Program
pages.stub_description: CS department graduate program overview, degree requirements summary, forms, contacts, and links to the full CS Graduate Handbook.
pages.bot_use: Primary reference for CS-specific program questions. Supplement with full handbook content.
